headline: United States wins 16th Presidents Cup: Scheffler and Cantlay lead 18.5-11.5 triumph at Medinah
whyCareReason: Team USA captures its 10th consecutive Presidents Cup at Medinah Course No. 3 as Scottie Scheffler and Patrick Cantlay lead a dominant Sunday singles performance.
teaser: FINAL: United States 18.5, International Team 11.5. Scheffler tops Matsuyama 3&2 and Cantlay closes out Scott 2&1 at Medinah No. 3.
story:
Why this one matters: The United States claimed its 10th consecutive Presidents Cup on Sunday afternoon, defeating the International Team 18.5 - 11.5 in front of packed galleries at Medinah Country Club.

Leading into Sunday singles, Captain Brandt Snedeker put his strongest anchors out early. World No. 1 Scottie Scheffler set the tone by defeating 2021 Masters champion Hideki Matsuyama 3&2. Patrick Cantlay followed with a clinical 2&1 triumph over veteran Adam Scott, who was playing in his record-tying 12th cup.

Xander Schauffele added another American point with a 4&3 victory over Sungjae Im, and Collin Morikawa secured a half-point against Min Woo Lee to push the United States comfortably past the 15.5-point victory threshold. Geoff Ogilvy's International Team fought valiantly on Medinah's redesigned Course No. 3, but the American depth proved insurmountable once again.
stakes: The United States retains the Presidents Cup trophy for the 10th consecutive time and improves its all-time series record to 14-1-1.
rivalryAngle: American dominance rolls on at Medinah as Chicago fans celebrate another cup triumph.
